anomalies.observed: The drawing shows R1 and R4 as 0 Ω links from the two servo signal paths to NET0024, so both servo signals are joined to the shared serial bus. The annotation instead says to short R13 and R14, but those are shown as 47 kΩ and 2.2 kΩ resistors in other parts of the circuit. The PWM signal paths also pass through R17 and R24 (1 kΩ) before reaching the servo headers.
anomalies.expected: PWM mode should keep the two servo signal pins on separate GPIO paths; serial mode should join them to the shared serial bus only by populating the specified R13/R14 jumpers. The schematic's actual jumper references and values should agree with that selection.

evidence.quote: Short R13, R14 for Serial Servo; R1 0; R4 0; R13 47k; R14 2.2k; R17 1k; R24 1k (page 1/1, sheet /)
PWM mode: each servo header's signal pin gets its own independent 1 kΩ-buffered GPIO line ... leave R13/R14 open; Serial mode: populate R13/R14 (page 1/1, sheet /)

anomalies.impact: As drawn, the servo signal paths are connected to the shared serial bus through the zero-ohm links rather than being independently selectable as specified. This can prevent independent PWM control and cause interference or contention between the PWM GPIOs and the serial interface.

parsed.summary: The servo-mode jumper implementation contradicts the specified routing: R1/R4 are shown as 0 Ω links into the shared serial bus, while the annotated R13/R14 positions are occupied by nonzero resistors elsewhere in the circuit. This joins the signal paths instead of providing the specified selectable PWM-versus-serial configuration.
